review: 1:1–1:2 — John 1:14 again; the stanza is only two lines in the print, so each couplet carries one sentence and ends on הַלְלוּיָהּ, which is left untranslated exactly as هَلِّلُويَا is.
2:1 קַדְמוֹן וָעֶד — 'the Ancient and Everlasting', for الْأَزَلِيّ وَالْأَبَدِيّ; the pair is the liturgical way of naming eternity past and future, which the Arabic's two adjectives distinguish.
4:1 נִשָּׂא הַדּוֹד עַל־צְלָב — 'the Beloved was lifted on a cross' (John 12:32, אִם אֶנָּשֵׂא); the Arabic رُفِعَ الْحَبِيب عَلَى الصَّلِيب is that lifting.
6:1 יָשַׁב הַנֶּאֱמָן לִימִין — Psalm 110:1 and Heb 10:12 (יָשַׁב לִימִין); the Arabic جَلَسَ الْأَمِين عَنِ الْيَمِين is the session, and לִימִין is the psalm's own preposition.
8:2 אֶת־עֲמִידָתֵנוּ — 'our waiting', for انْتِظَارَنَا; עֲמִידָה is the post-biblical noun for standing/awaiting, used because a longer clause would break the two-line stanza.
